The average salaries of vice-chancellors have reached a new high.
The premiers of New South Wales and Victoria met to discuss health reforms.

tags.specification: Check official titles in reliable reference sources; capitalise official titles of specific individuals, lower-case generic/plural references.
tags.violation_condition: the official title of a principal or chief executive of an Australian institution written in lower case, or a general reference not referring to a specific person written with initial capitals

when: Use lower case for most of these titles in general references that do not refer to a specific person.
rules.why: G-2: Consolidates principal titles capitalisation and generic exception.

anchor.quote: Use initial capitals for formal names connected with parliament. Generic references are in lower case.

parts.quote: Parliament House
There was a change to parliamentary procedures.

tags.violation_condition: a formal name connected with parliament written in lower case, or a generic reference capitalised

rules.why: Covers general parliamentary formal names vs generic references.

anchor.quote: Use initial capitals for the formal titles of parliamentary office holders.

parts.quote: Senator Lines is the Deputy President and Chair of Committees in the 46th Parliament.

tags.violation_condition: the formal title of a parliamentary office holder (e.g. Clerk of the House, Speaker of the House) written in lower case

rules.why: Covers formal titles of parliamentary office holders.

anchor.quote: Use initial capitals for the formal titles of current members of parliament.

covers.quote: Use lower case for parliamentary terms that are not formal titles.

parts.quote: Mr Adam Bandt MP
Senator Pauline Hanson
She moved from the backbench to take the new ministerial portfolio.
He was a former senator for Tasmania, serving from 1947 to 1951.

tags.violation_condition: the formal title of a current member of parliament written in lower case, or parliamentary terms that are not formal titles capitalised

when: Use lower case for parliamentary terms that are not formal titles (e.g. member of parliament, senator, frontbench, backbencher, crossbencher).
rules.why: G-2: Consolidates titles of members of parliament with non-formal parliamentary terms.
